first_impression.reaction: My assistant found this when I said I wanted to keep my words short. The first screen is quiet and well written: no gushing, no prices, no packages. Her summary: 'Twenty sample vows, the Australian legal wording, a short template, sensible delivery notes. Written for couples doing it themselves. Nothing on large ceremonies, privacy or other traditions.' I read the intro and takeaways, glanced at the classic and destination examples, then read the delivery notes and the close. I skipped the funny ones.

journey.quote: Many would rather say something true, say it well and hand the moment back to the ceremony.
journey.reaction: Yes. With three hundred people watching, I don't want a speech. This is the right instinct and it's said with restraint.

journey.quote: If you marry legally overseas, the legal wording follows that country, so ask your celebrant or registrar early.
journey.reaction: Correct and useful. Our families are across three countries, so where the legal part happens is a real decision for us.

journey.quote: In New Zealand, couples can write their own vows as long as each says words to the effect of "I [name] take you [name] to be my legal wife/husband/partner".
journey.reaction: The only overseas example is New Zealand. Nothing on the UAE or the UK, which is where my questions are. I'd need to ask a planner.

journey.quote: Your celebrant or registrar sets the words; the place, the guests and the travel are the bigger puzzle.
journey.reaction: That's true, and it's the part I care about. But nothing here shows they've solved that puzzle for four hundred guests flying in from three continents.

journey.quote: Thank you to everyone who crossed oceans to be here.
journey.reaction: This line I'd actually use. Half our guests will fly in from Sydney and London.

journey.quote: I vow to share the remote, to learn the name of every plant you bring home, and to never again say 'it's only a short drive' when it isn't.
journey.reaction: Charming for some couples, but not for a ceremony in front of our elders. Skipped it.

journey.section: What are some good short wedding vows?
journey.quote: Each of these is our own writing, and yours to adapt.
journey.reaction: Good that it's original and not lifted from somewhere. But the whole set assumes a Western exchange of personal vows. Many ceremonies in our world don't work that way, and the page doesn't acknowledge that.

journey.section: How do you say your vows with confidence?
journey.quote: Ask your venue whether a microphone is available for the ceremony, who sets it up, and whether you can test it at the rehearsal.
journey.reaction: The right concern, but at our scale it's a full sound crew and production company, not whether the venue has a microphone. It reads like advice for a garden wedding of sixty.

journey.section: Saying it in your own words
journey.quote: Where you say them, and who flies in to hear them, is where a Wedded Advisor comes in.
journey.reaction: A nice close, and one contact means fewer people who know our plans. Still, it's a blog link, not an introduction.

unanswered_questions: Have you delivered ceremonies for 200 to 400 guests, with production-grade sound, and can you show me one discreetly? (deferred business detail)
Can you work with ceremonies where the formal vows follow a faith or family tradition, and fit personal words around them? (deferred business detail)
What are the legal ceremony requirements if we marry in the UAE or the UK rather than Australia or New Zealand?
How do you protect privacy at the ceremony: no guest phones, NDAs for celebrant, crew and photographers, nothing posted? (deferred business detail)
Can the ceremony location be closed to the public and other hotel guests? (deferred business detail)
Can you work through a family office and in currencies other than AUD? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: Reading from a card is entirely normal and takes the pressure off. Write your vows on a small, sturdy card in large print.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. Mildly patronising for someone who speaks in public regularly. Written for a nervous first-timer, not for me.

turn_offs_found.quote: Our dog approved of you before I did, and she has excellent judgement.
turn_offs_found.why: Cute, standard-client content. It makes the page feel like it's for everyone, which means it isn't for me.

would_share_with: My assistant would send the legal section and the destination examples to our planner and celebrant. Nobody else.

cta_reaction.quote: Through [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=short-wedding-vows&utm_content=primary), one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact.
cta_reaction.why: The tone is calm and the single point of contact appeals for discretion. But I don't enquire from a blog post about sample vows, and nothing here shows scale, privacy or cultural depth. I'd want a private introduction.

top_3_changes: Add one line acknowledging that many ceremonies follow faith or family traditions for the formal vows, and that personal words can sit alongside them, phrased without stereotyping and without brand claims that need sourcing.
Widen the delivery note on sound beyond 'whether a microphone is available' to cover large ceremonies: amplification for several hundred guests and who runs it.
Add a short privacy note for the ceremony itself, such as agreeing a phone-free ceremony or what the photographer and guests may share, since the vows are the most private words of the day.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Layla (uhnw): assistant-first skim, judged from the first screen, looked for scale, discretion and cultural awareness, put off by over-explaining and generic content
No invented brand facts; scale proof, tradition handling, confidentiality, exclusive use and currency listed in unanswered_questions as deferred
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: A sample-vows post is structurally low relevance for Layla; the low enquiry score reflects the topic, not a copy defect. The draft is clean and understated, with no broken sentences or price language. The main persona-specific gaps are cultural acknowledgement and ceremony privacy.

assumptions: Layla's assistant found the post and summarised it; Layla read the intro, takeaways, classic and destination examples, delivery notes and the close, and skipped the light and funny section.
The persona is provisional and not calibrated with the CRM, so confidence is 0.75.
Deferred business details are not penalised in the scores beyond noting that they are missing.
